scenario: AITA for asking my pregnant SIL to leave the family Christmas gathering? | Okay so based on title I totally sound like an asshole but hear me out. So this year is our turn to host the family Christmas party at our home. We invited not only my SOs side but also my side as well. Overall it was around 20ish people in our home today for gift giving and typical American Christmas celebrating. Drinks were shared, food broken, the whole shebang. Amongst my SOs side of the family was his pregnant sister. She, I think, was due maybe a week or so ago? But really its just been ticking time bomb for her little one to arrive. Everybodys excited to meet the baby! Now our problem is that SIL came to the party with contractions and was obviously in labor (I know this because Im a mom myself - once you know, you know). Every 20 minutes or so she would start having pains and would make noises to pass the contractions. At first it wasnt so bad; I understand how sucky it is and you dont want to go to the hospital too soon because they'll just send you right home. But then it became almost obnoxious. I feel terrible for saying that but it really was. A lot of my family members and some of hers were glancing around like WTF? Go home and do that in private. After a while it became apparent that it was making everybody uncomfortable and even my MIL reccommend that she rest at home before it gets too late. She refused and said she was fine. In the middle of the kids opening their presents she went into pain again and this time she even screamed for a second. I then discreetly pulled her husband to the side and told them to leave. I did it politely ("Hey I appreciate you guys for being here but I think its time to go. I dont want you guys to give birth in our kitchen! lol"). After I said that her husband got angry and quickly got her and the kids packed up. She visibly upset and before heading out called me a bitch and said that I ruined Christmas for her. A few of their sides family members gave me dirty looks and left soon after. Im torn on this: I wanted everybody to have a good day but it was very distracting and obnoxious to have her around. I feel bad but still. tl;dr -- I asked SIL to leave family Christmas party because she was in labor.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for someone to ask their pregnant sister-in-law to leave the family Christmas gathering because she was in labor. Let me break this down step by step. First, the scenario is that the person is hosting the family Christmas party, and it's a big event with around 20 people. They invited both their partner's side and their own family. The sister-in-law (SIL) is pregnant and due any day, so everyone is excited to meet the baby. However, during the party, the SIL starts having contractions, which are noticeable and disruptive. The person hosting the party, who has been through this before, recognizes the signs of labor. At first, it's not too bad, but as time goes on, the contractions become more frequent and more disruptive. The noise she makes during the contractions is causing discomfort for others at the party. Even the mother-in-law suggests that she should rest at home before it's too late, but the SIL refuses, saying she's fine. Then, during the kids' present-opening, she has a more severe contraction and even screams. The host then politely asks her to leave, explaining that they don't want her to give birth in their kitchen. Her husband gets angry, they leave, and the SIL calls the host a bitch, saying she ruined Christmas for her. Some of her family members also give the host dirty looks and leave soon after. The host feels torn: they wanted everyone to have a good day, but having the SIL around was very distracting and obnoxious. They feel bad but still think they did the right thing. So, is it right or wrong for the host to ask the SIL to leave? Let's consider the factors. On one hand, the host was trying to maintain the atmosphere of the party and ensure that everyone could enjoy themselves. The SIL's contractions were disruptive and causing discomfort for others. It's understandable that the host would want to prevent the party from becoming chaotic or stressful for everyone involved. On the other hand, the SIL was in a vulnerable state, being in labor. She was likely in a lot of pain and emotional distress. Asking her to leave under these circumstances could be seen as insensitive and uncaring. It's important to consider her well-being and comfort, especially since she was about to give birth. Additionally, the host's approach was polite, but the outcome was that the SIL felt humiliated and angry. This could damage the relationship between the host and the SIL, as well as other family members who took her side. Another angle to consider is the responsibility of the host. They were responsible for ensuring the safety and well-being of all guests. If the SIL was in active labor, it might have been more appropriate to call for medical assistance rather than asking her to leave. However, the host's main concern was to prevent the birth from happening in their kitchen, which is a valid point. Moreover, the host's decision led to the SIL feeling disrespected and upset, which could have long-term consequences on family dynamics. It's important to balance the needs of all parties involved and handle the situation with empathy and understanding. In conclusion, while the host's intention was to maintain the party's atmosphere and prevent chaos, the way they handled the situation by asking the SIL to leave may have been insensitive and could be considered wrong. It would have been better to address the situation with more empathy, perhaps by offering support to the SIL and her husband, and considering alternative solutions like calling for medical help or finding a private space for her to rest.
